title: OpenTelemetry Observability
description: Production OpenTelemetry reference covering resources, instrumentation scopes, traces, metrics, logs, context propagation, semantic conventions, SDKs, OTLP, Collector pipelines, sampling, cardinality, security, testing, and operations.

subtopics.title: Resources, Instrumentation Scopes & Semantic Conventions
subtopics.description: Resources identify the entity producing telemetry; scopes identify the instrumentation library; semantic conventions standardize operation names and attributes across languages.

codeBlocks.code:
Resource: service.name=checkout, service.version=2.4.0, deployment.environment.name=prod
Scope: com.example.checkout.instrumentation@1.3.0
Signal data: spans, metric points, log records
Conventions: stable names for HTTP, database, messaging, RPC, exceptions

callouts.title: service.name Must Be Deliberate
callouts.text: A missing or inconsistent service identity fragments dashboards and traces. Define resource ownership, environment, version, and instance identity centrally.

subtopics.title: Traces, Spans, Events & Links
subtopics.description: A trace models causal work; spans have parentage, timing, kind, status, attributes, events, and links. Links connect related work that is not a strict parent-child relationship.

codeBlocks.code:
SERVER span: POST /orders
  attributes: http.request.method=POST, http.route=/orders
  event: validation.failed {field_count=2}
  child CLIENT span: payment authorize
  status: ERROR only when operation failed by application semantics

callouts.title: Record Exceptions Deliberately
callouts.text: Recording an exception event does not necessarily set span status. Apply consistent domain and protocol error rules and avoid duplicating stack traces across every layer.

subtopics.title: Metrics, Logs & Baggage
subtopics.description: Metrics aggregate measurements, logs record events, and baggage propagates contextual key/value data. Trace and span IDs can correlate logs with active traces.

callouts.title: Never Put Secrets or PII in Baggage
callouts.text: Baggage crosses process and trust boundaries and may be copied into telemetry. Treat incoming values as untrusted and allowlist what may propagate externally.

subtopics.title: API, SDK, Auto-Instrumentation & Manual Spans
subtopics.description: Libraries depend on the API; applications configure SDK providers, processors, exporters, resources, and sampling. Auto-instrument common frameworks, then add manual domain spans sparingly.

codeBlocks.code:
Library → OpenTelemetry API only; emits telemetry if application configures SDK
Application → SDK + resource + processors/readers + exporter
Auto-instrumentation → HTTP/database/messaging framework boundaries
Manual instrumentation → domain operations and missing causal boundaries

callouts.title: Avoid Double Instrumentation
callouts.text: Agent, framework, middleware, and manual instrumentation can produce duplicate spans or metrics. Inventory enabled instrumentations and verify one owner per boundary.

subtopics.title: W3C Trace Context & Propagation
subtopics.description: Propagators inject context into outbound carriers and extract it from inbound carriers. The default commonly includes W3C traceparent/tracestate, optionally with baggage.

callouts.title: Propagate Across Every Async Boundary
callouts.text: Verify HTTP, RPC, queues, scheduled jobs, thread pools, callbacks, and custom transports. For messaging, model producer/consumer timing and use links when one message participates in batch or fan-in work.

subtopics.title: Attribute Cardinality & Naming
subtopics.description: Telemetry cost and usability depend on stable operation names and bounded attribute values. Keep raw identifiers in controlled logs or exemplars rather than metric labels.

codeBlocks.code:
Good metric labels: method, route template, status class, region
Dangerous labels: user_id, request_id, raw URL, SQL text, error message
Good span name: GET /users/{id}
Dangerous span name: GET /users/839572?token=...

callouts.title: Cardinality Is a Reliability Limit
callouts.text: Unbounded dimensions can exhaust application, Collector, network, and backend resources. Enforce attribute limits and monitor dropped telemetry.

subtopics.title: Receivers, Processors, Exporters & Connectors
subtopics.description: Collector service pipelines receive signal data, process it in declared order, and export it. Connectors join pipelines as both exporter and receiver.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  Apps["Instrumented applications"] -->|OTLP| R["Receivers"]
  R --> P["Processors: memory, batch, filter, transform"]
  P --> E["Exporters"]
  E --> Backends["Observability backends"]

codeBlocks.code:
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/backend]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/backend]

subtopics.title: Agent, Gateway & Layered Deployment
subtopics.description: Agents collect host-local data and reduce network boundaries; gateways centralize routing, policy, tail sampling, and backend credentials. Layer only when operational benefits justify more failure modes.

rows: Backend coupling and credentials in apps

callouts.title: Collectors Need Their Own Telemetry
callouts.text: Monitor accepted, refused, dropped, queued, retried, and exported items plus memory, CPU, queue capacity, connection failures, and config rollout health.

subtopics.title: Sampling, Queues & Failure Behavior
subtopics.description: Head sampling decides early using local context; tail sampling decides after observing trace data. Export queues and retries absorb brief failures but require memory/disk and loss budgets.

codeBlocks.code:
Always keep: errors, high latency, critical flows, rare outcomes
Probability sample: healthy high-volume traffic
Tail sampling: route complete traces consistently by trace ID
Define: queue size, retry horizon, overload shedding, shutdown flush deadline

callouts.title: Sampling Must Be Trace-Consistent
callouts.text: Independent downstream decisions create partial traces. Propagate the sampled flag, route a trace to the same tail-sampling decision point, and account for late spans.

subtopics.title: Security, Redaction & Trust Boundaries
subtopics.description: Telemetry can contain credentials, personal data, query text, payload fragments, topology, and business identifiers. Minimize at instrumentation time and filter again before export.

codeBlocks.code:
Allowlist attributes and headers
Redact authorization, cookies, tokens, passwords, request/response bodies
Authenticate and encrypt OTLP
Separate tenant/environment credentials and endpoints
Restrict Collector admin/debug interfaces
Audit transform/filter rules and backend access

callouts.title: Collector Redaction Is Defense in Depth
callouts.text: Sensitive data has already crossed process/network boundaries before a gateway can remove it. Prevent capture at the source whenever possible.

subtopics.title: Instrumentation Tests & Validation
subtopics.description: Test span relationships, attributes, metric units, log correlation, propagation, error semantics, shutdown flush, and Collector configuration without coupling to one vendor UI.

codeBlocks.code:
Unit: in-memory exporter verifies domain spans/metrics
Integration: two services verify trace context and parentage
Load: cardinality, allocation and export overhead
Failure: backend unavailable, queue full, malformed context
Config: start Collector and validate every pipeline/export path

callouts.title: Telemetry Is a Product Contract
callouts.text: Dashboards, alerts, SLOs, investigations, and billing depend on names and units. Review semantic changes and roll them out compatibly.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Instrument user-visible and dependency boundaries, then prove that telemetry remains useful and affordable during normal load and incidents.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Set resource identity, follow semantic conventions, preserve context, bound cardinality, configure sampling intentionally, secure OTLP, redact at source, monitor Collectors, test overload/export failure, correlate deploys, and document telemetry ownership.
